styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a modern shuttered storefront, which is a different subject from the references' tiled-roof houses but still the same kind (a whole building). The measured facts are close to the references: 9 visible tones per tile against 10-12, 0% neutral dark edge pixels so the outlines are tinted, and 13% near-flat coverage against 0%. The picture is shallower than the facts suggest. Each material has only about 3 lightness steps. The grey wall panels, the blue sign board and the roller shutter are large areas of one flat colour with only thin horizontal slat lines, and the sign is a flat blue slab with a light border. The references use 5-6 steps with per-tile highlights, plaster speckle and stones shaded one by one. The candidate has no comparable grain, speckle or per-element highlights, so it reads cleaner and flatter, closer to a vector or sticker look. The 13% flat coverage confirms the flat fills against the references' 0%. The outline is a dark blue-grey tone, tinted rather than black, which is acceptable. Overall it is below the Beodeul standard for shading depth and texture.

The measured facts are close to the references: 9 visible tones per tile against 10-12, and 0% near-neutral dark edges, so the outlines carry a tint (bluish and grey-brown) rather than a black sticker line. answer.evidence: The whole shopfront is a flat south elevation: a 2-row light parapet rim at rows 15-16, a window/terrace panel, a sill band at rows 47-50, a wall with windows, a front-facing cornice strip at rows 79-82, a sign, and a shutter. No roof slope, no ellipse, no awning plane, and no edge line with an eave shadow is seen. The ledges are 1-4 row strips and the lintels over the windows are flat strips. The plants and notice are decor. No horizontal top surface is drawn, so the object reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a modern vacant-shop facade: a gray-blue stacked building with a sign band, shutter and a window. The references are timber and stone houses with tile roofs. Both are buildings, so the kind matches. Measured facts are mostly close: 9 visible tones per tile against 10-12 for the references, near-flat coverage 13% against 0%, and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outlines are tinted. By eye, the shading is shallow, with about 4 steps on the wall and shutter against 5-6 on the references. The sign panel is a large flat blue fill with only a white glyph. The shutter has some horizontal slat lines, but the surfaces are flat and clean rather than grainy. Texture is sparse, with no per-tile highlights or speckle, and it is not as dense as the roof tile and stone work in the references. Because 13% of the area is flat fill and the shading is shallower than both references, the piece reads as flatter and more sticker-like, so it fails.
